title: Clarification Timing Does Not Mitigate Anchoring Bias in Tool-Using LLM Agents

contributions.purpose: Test whether forcing clarification before retrieval exposure mitigates anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents.
contributions.mechanism: Controlled three-condition experiment (search-first baseline, IRG clarify-first, candidate-order control) on InteractComp-Anchor (210 instances) with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct under identical interaction budgets and pre-registered success criteria.
contributions.evaluation: Negative result: the Intent Reconstruction Gate (IRG) yields a negligible +0.95pp over the search-first baseline (p=0.42).
contributions.domain: Anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents
contributions.source_quote: The first controlled test of whether clarification timing can mitigate anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents, with pre-registered success criteria.

contributions.purpose: Identify the dominant causal factor in anchoring bias for tool-using agents.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of the timing intervention against a candidate-order control in which the target candidate is simply listed first.
contributions.evaluation: Reordering candidates achieves 13.33pp gains (p<0.001), 14x more effective than the IRG intervention; presentation order, not clarification timing, dominates.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical evidence that candidate presentation order dominates timing effects: reordering candidates is 14x more effective than the IRG intervention.

contributions.purpose: Give practitioners actionable guidance for mitigating anchoring bias in deployed agents.
contributions.mechanism: Recommendation derived from the experimental results: prioritize candidate presentation strategies such as randomization and confidence-based reordering.
contributions.evaluation: Backed by the 13.33pp vs +0.95pp contrast between reordering and clarification-timing interventions.
contributions.source_quote: Actionable guidance for practitioners: focus on candidate presentation strategies (e.g., randomization, confidence-based reordering) rather than clarification timing to mitigate anchoring bias.

self_declared_provenance.quote: This approach is motivated by cognitive science research showing that anchoring effects can be mitigated through deliberation before anchor exposure (Sumita et al., 2024).

While prior work has focused primarily on detecting and characterizing these biases, mitigation strategies remain underexplored, particularly in agentic settings where models interact with external tools and information sources.
Our work builds on this foundation by conducting the first controlled test of whether clarification timing can mitigate anchoring bias in tool-using agents.

notes: Explicit negative-result paper: the tested IRG intervention does not work (+0.95pp, p=0.42); all three contributions are findings from the null result, no new method is claimed to succeed.
